title: Localization of big etale derived direct image and base-change compatibility
statement:
Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use compatible small presentations of the big etale sites $B_V=(\mathrm{Sch}/V)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and small etale sites $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$ in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention, lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. Write $\mathrm{Ab}(C)$ for abelian sheaves on a site $C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a scheme map $a:V\to W$, let $a_s:\mathrm{Sh}(V_{\mathrm{Et}})\to\mathrm{Sh}(W_{\mathrm{Et}})$ be its small-site morphism and $a_b:\mathrm{Sh}(B_V)\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_W)$ the big-site morphism, with $(a_b^{-1}H)(U/V)=H(U/W)$. Let $g:S'\to S$ be any object of $B_S$ and form the cartesian square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}T'&\xrightarrow{g'}&T\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\ S'&\xrightarrow{g}&S.\end{array}$$
The continuous and cocontinuous functors $u_g:S'_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_S$, $(U\to S')\mapsto(U\to S)$, and $u_{g'}:T'_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_T$ induce geometric morphisms $i_g:\mathrm{Sh}(S'_{\mathrm{Et}})\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_S)$ and $i_{g'}:\mathrm{Sh}(T'_{\mathrm{Et}})\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_T)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Their exact inverse images are small-site restriction: $(i_g^{-1}H)(U/S')=H(U/S)$, and likewise for $i_{g'}$. If $i_{S'}$ denotes $i_{\mathrm{id}_{S'}}$, then $i_g=g_b\circ i_{S'}$, while $\pi_S\circ i_g\cong g_s$ and $\pi_T\circ i_{g'}\cong g'_s$.
For every $M\in D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(B_T))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], the canonical derived restriction and localization comparisons are natural isomorphisms
$$c_{g,M}:i_g^{-1}Rf_{b,*}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_{s,*}(i_{g'}^{-1}M)\quad\text{in }D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(S'_{\mathrm{Et}})),$$
$$\ell_{g,M}:g_b^{-1}Rf_{b,*}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_{b,*}((g'_b)^{-1}M)\quad\text{in }D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(B_{S'})).$$
Here $i_g^{-1}$ is restriction to a small site, whereas $g_b^{-1}$ is localization to the big site over $S'$. The comparisons are the derived adjunction-mate comparisons for these squares. More explicitly, let $K\in D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(T_{\mathrm{Et}}))$ and let
$$\beta_K:\pi_S^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\longrightarrow Rf_{b,*}\pi_T^{-1}K$$
be the canonical mate for $\pi_S\circ f_b\cong f_s\circ\pi_T$ [def-trf-topos-derived-base-change-map]. Under $i_g^{-1}\pi_S^{-1}\cong g_s^{-1}$, $c_{g,\pi_T^{-1}K}$, and $i_{g'}^{-1}\pi_T^{-1}\cong(g'_s)^{-1}$, the morphism $i_g^{-1}\beta_K$ is exactly the small-site derived exchange
$$g_s^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\longrightarrow Rf'_{s,*}(g'_s)^{-1}K$$
with its counit-transpose normalization [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. The family of all $i_g^{-1}$, for all objects $g:S'\to S$ of $B_S$, is jointly conservative on $D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(B_S))$.

proof.text: For $u_g:S'_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_S$, a small covering is sent to the identical jointly surjective etale family, and fibre products along covering members are the same scheme fibre products [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Conversely, a big covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ of $U\to S'$ etale lifts to the small site: give $V_j$ its composite map to $S'$, etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2). Thus $u_g$ is continuous and cocontinuous. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction]: it gives $i_g$ with inverse image the restriction $H\mapsto(U\mapsto H(U/S))$. Apply the same argument to $g'$. Lift these adjunctions to abelian group objects with [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects] and [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects]. Exactness of abelian inverse images follows from [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$: every abelian group has its unique integer-module structure.

source.place: Topologies Tag 021F, lemma-put-in-T-etale; Sites Tag 00XR, lemma-when-shriek

proof.text: For any $a:V\to W$, the forgetful functor $v_a:B_V\to B_W$ is continuous and cocontinuous: it sends a covering to itself, preserves fibre products along coverings, and a covering of $U/W$ with $U/V$ lifts by composition with $U\to V$. The same continuous-cocontinuous adjunction gives $a_b^{-1}H(U/V)=H(U/W)$. Its right adjoint has the formula $a_{b,*}F(U/W)=F(U\times_WV/V)$. Indeed the compatible families in the right-adjoint formula of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] are determined by their member at $U\times_WV\to U$: every pair $(A/V,A\to U/W)$ factors uniquely through this pair by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Conversely that member gives the family by restriction. This works for morphisms and abelian sheaves via the lifted adjunction of step 1. The unit is restriction along $U\times_WV\to U$, and the counit at $A/V$ is restriction along the graph $A\to A\times_WV$.

source.place: Topologies Tag 021H, lemma-morphism-big-etale (including its right-adjoint construction)

proof.text: For the small inclusion $V_{\mathrm{Et}}\hookrightarrow B_V$, apply [lem-trf-bigger-site-retraction]. Continuity and cocontinuity were checked in step 1 for $g=\mathrm{id}_V$; it is fully faithful because both categories use all $V$-morphisms, preserves the fibre products of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and sends the final object $V/V$ to $V/V$. Thus it supplies $i_V$ and $\pi_V$ with $i_V^{-1}=\pi_{V,*}$ and $\pi_V i_V\cong\mathrm{id}$. Restriction on abelian sheaves is exactly the exact functor of [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. The section formulas give $i_g^{-1}=i_{S'}^{-1}g_b^{-1}$, hence $i_g=g_b i_{S'}$ with the canonical adjunction identification. Also, on every small etale $U/W$, both $\pi_{W,*}a_{b,*}F$ and $a_{s,*}\pi_{V,*}F$ are $F(U\times_WV/V)$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. These natural direct-image identities give $\pi_Wa_b\cong a_s\pi_V$ by [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Therefore $\pi_Si_g\cong g_s$ and $\pi_Ti_{g'}\cong g'_s$.

source.place: Topologies Tags 021G and 021I, lemma-at-the-bottom-etale and lemma-morphism-big-small-etale

proof.text: The slice $B_W/(V\to W)$ is the big site $B_V$: an object is a $W$-scheme $U$ with a $W$-map to $V$, equivalently a $V$-scheme, with exactly the same morphisms and coverings. Thus $a_b^{-1}$ is localized-site restriction. It is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact] and preserves injectives by [new-over-pullback-preserves-injectives]. For $i_V^{-1}=\pi_{V,*}$, use the abelian adjunction $\pi_V^{-1}\dashv\pi_{V,*}$ (step 1's lift for the retraction datum) and exactness of $\pi_V^{-1}$ from [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] with $\mathbf Z$. The Mathlib leaf [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] then shows that $\pi_{V,*}$ preserves injectives, because an exact functor preserves monomorphisms. Consequently $i_g^{-1}=\pi_{S',*}g_b^{-1}$ and $i_{g'}^{-1}=\pi_{T',*}g_b'^{-1}$ preserve injectives as well as being exact. This is the abelian-sheaf argument; no assertion about structure-sheaf-module injectives is used.

source.place: Tag 0758, lemma-compare-injectives (abelian case); Cohomology on Sites Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open

proof.text: Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $B_T$. For $U\to S'$ small etale, the two sheaves $i_g^{-1}f_{b,*}F$ and $f'_{s,*}i_{g'}^{-1}F$ both have sections $F(U\times_{S'}T'/T)=F(U\times_ST/T)$, with identical restrictions, by the cartesian fibre-product identity and the formulas of steps 1–2 and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This gives a natural underived isomorphism $c^0_g$. For any $U/S'$ (without an etaleness restriction), the same calculation gives the natural isomorphism $\ell^0_g:g_b^{-1}f_{b,*}\cong f'_{b,*}g_b'^{-1}$. The equality of fibre products is the unique map commuting with both projections [def-pc-fibre-product], so these are the specified section comparisons.

Choose a bounded-below complex $I$ of injective abelian sheaves representing $M$, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. By step 4 both $i_{g'}^{-1}I$ and $g_b'^{-1}I$ are bounded-below complexes of injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective](2): the four derived direct images occurring in the comparisons are represented respectively by $f_{b,*}I$, $f'_{s,*}i_{g'}^{-1}I$, and $f'_{b,*}g_b'^{-1}I$. Exact restriction is applied termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Hence the termwise isomorphisms $c^0_g(I)$ and $\ell^0_g(I)$ of step 5 give $c_{g,M}$ and $\ell_{g,M}$. For a derived morphism choose its homotopy-class representative between injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the underived isomorphisms commute with that representative. Additive functors preserve homotopies, so this proves naturality and independence of representatives.

Fix the mate normalization carefully. The mate of $c_g^0$ has inverse-image direction $\sigma_g:f_s'^{-1}i_g^{-1}\to i_{g'}^{-1}f_b^{-1}$. This need not be an isomorphism. It is the adjunct of $c^0_{g,f_b^{-1}H}\circ i_g^{-1}(\eta_{f_b,H})$ under $f_s'^{-1}\dashv f'_{s,*}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The units and counits here are the actual sheaf adjunctions of steps 1–3. The localization comparison $\ell_g^0$ is similarly the mate of the canonical big-site inverse-image square, which is an isomorphism: both composite restrictions send $H$ to $(U/T')\mapsto H(U/S)$. Apply [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-mate-model] with $L=f_b^{-1}$, $L'=f_s'^{-1}$, $G=i_g^{-1}$, $H=i_{g'}^{-1}$, and then with $L'=f_b'^{-1}$, $G=g_b^{-1}$, $H=g_b'^{-1}$. All four left/square functors are exact, and both source sheaf categories have enough injectives. On $I$ the source and target right-derived comparison units are invertible by step 6. Thus its equation identifies the derived mates precisely with $c^0_g(I)$ and $\ell^0_g(I)$, so the isomorphisms of step 6 have the required canonical normalization.

For the arrow clause, denote the inverse-image identification for $\beta$ by $\theta:f_b^{-1}\pi_S^{-1}\cong\pi_T^{-1}f_s^{-1}$. It is the canonical composition identification of $\pi_S f_b\cong f_s\pi_T$ in step 3. Paste $\sigma_g\pi_S^{-1}$ with $i_{g'}^{-1}\theta$. Under $i_g^{-1}\pi_S^{-1}\cong g_s^{-1}$ and $i_{g'}^{-1}\pi_T^{-1}\cong g_s'^{-1}$ this is the canonical map $f_s'^{-1}g_s^{-1}\cong g_s'^{-1}f_s^{-1}$. To check its normalization, transpose before deriving: $\sigma_g$ was defined using $i_g^{-1}\eta_{f_b}$ and the identity $c_g^0$ on the section $U\times_ST$. The conjugate defining $\theta$ uses the identity $\pi_{S,*}f_{b,*}=f_{s,*}\pi_{T,*}$ on that same section. The two adjunct constructions cancel the intervening unit/counit by $f_{b,*}\varepsilon_{f_b}\circ\eta_{f_b}f_{b,*}=1$. What remains is the fibre-product map $(U\times_SS')\times_{S'}T'\cong U\times_ST'$, which defines the small-site composition comparison. Thus the pasted map is the specified small square, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism. The cancellation is the conjugate/pasting rule [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1),(3); exact termwise descent preserves this identity by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exact-square-factorization].

source.place: Tag 0DDJ, lemma-compare-higher-direct-image-proper, proof of (2); Topologies Tag 021I

proof.text:
Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1) to the two derived squares just identified. The mate of their pasted inverse-image square is
$$c_{g,\pi_T^{-1}K}\circ i_g^{-1}(\beta_K).$$
Here $\beta_K$ is exactly the counit-transpose mate of [def-trf-topos-derived-base-change-map] with constant ring $\mathbf Z$. By step 8 the pasted square is the canonical small inverse-image square. Therefore its mate is the small-site exchange of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]: its transpose is $f_s'^{-1}g_s^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\to g_s'^{-1}f_s^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\xrightarrow{g_s'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f_s,K}}g_s'^{-1}K$. This gives the asserted equality of arrows under the three stated comparisons, for every bounded-below $K$. No properness or torsion was used; these belong only to the parent comparison theorem.

The family of restrictions detects zero abelian sheaves: if $i_g^{-1}A=0$ for every $g:S'\to S$, evaluation at the final small object $S'/S'$ gives $A(S'/S)=0$; these are all big-site objects, so $A=0$. For a complex $N$, exactness gives $i_g^{-1}H^r(N)=H^r(i_g^{-1}N)$ by applying restriction to the kernel/image quotient defining cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence if all restrictions of $QN$ are zero, every cohomology sheaf of $N$ is zero, and $0\to N$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $QN=0$ in the derived localization. For an arbitrary derived morphism $z$, take a distinguished cone triangle. Exact restriction is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; if each $i_g^{-1}z$ is invertible its cone is zero by [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero]. The preceding zero-object argument makes the original cone zero, and that same cone criterion makes $z$ invertible. This proves joint conservativity on $D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(B_S))$.
